excerpt: V1 events are retained unchanged. Their companyId requirement and restricted update vocabulary are incompatible with the requested M1A model. New estate-service events use events/v2 and agrosphere.<EventType>.v2 routing on agrosphere.domain. V2 envelopes use occurredAt and sourceService plus explicit provenance and full versioned entity snapshots. No company identifier is fabricated, and v1 consumers receive no silent schema change. Consumers must explicitly upgrade bindings/projections before integration. This is an independently versioned 0.2.0 contract release; no source dependency or automatic release/push is introduced.

head: 7e962552421f15ad5d1492276817db1e1692b104
excerpt: Consumer transaction: insert (consumer_name,event_id) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; apply projection only when inserted, in the same transaction; commit before ACK. Publisher writes outbox with domain mutation; relay publishes persistent messages with confirms and marks published only after confirmation. Duplicates are expected. Bounded retries and DLQ handling are required before consumers ship. Estate Service implements its v2 relay in Milestone 1A; consumer handlers remain separate work. Validate forecast period ordering and business semantics in applications as JSON Schema cannot enforce them.

excerpt: Estate OpenAPI now defines sixteen business operations and Problem Details, JWT scope, pagination and optimistic versions. Four new self-contained events/v2 snapshot schemas use occurredAt/sourceService, canonical estateId/entityId and optional blockId as applicable. Every v1 contract remains byte-for-byte preserved. Estate Service publishes only v2; existing v1 consumers must explicitly migrate to agrosphere.<EventType>.v2. There is no dual publishing.

head: 7fdd691431a6962f5ac71fb08e9e3e09380bae00
excerpt: V1 is unchanged. V2 creates estate, division, plantation_block and rubber_clone, and extends outbox_event with delivery status and retry scheduling. head: 7fdd691431a6962f5ac71fb08e9e3e09380bae00
excerpt: Domain writes and mandatory outbox inserts share one JPA-managed database transaction. The dispatcher locks due rows with SKIP LOCKED and sends persistent mandatory messages to durable agrosphere.domain using publisher confirms. Returns, nacks and exceptions retry with configurable exponential backoff; exhausted events remain FAILED for operator-controlled replay. Publication defaults disabled while preserving outbox records. Confirmation/crash ambiguity permits duplicates with the same eventId. Consumers must deduplicate consumer_name/eventId transactionally, ACK after commit and reject stale revisions. No exactly-once delivery is claimed. The implementation follows the [Spring AMQP confirm/return API](https://docs.spring.io/spring-amqp/reference/amqp/template.html).

excerpt: Business routes are authenticated by default. Nimbus validates RS256 signatures, configured issuer, lifetime and estate-service audience. Trusted Keycloak-style realm_access.roles supplies PLATFORM_ADMIN, ESTATE_ADMIN, ESTATE_MANAGER and VIEWER. Signed, administrator-managed estate_ids scopes reads/writes. Client headers or user-editable attributes are not treated as grants. PLATFORM_ADMIN alone creates estates/clones and has global scope; estate admins/managers write assigned estates; viewers read assigned estates. Lists apply scope in SQL before counting/pagination. Only health routes are public. No production credentials are hardcoded. See [Spring Security JWT validation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/oauth2/resource-server/jwt.html) and the service runbook.

head: 7fdd691431a6962f5ac71fb08e9e3e09380bae00
excerpt: Implement AgroSphere Milestone 1B Spatial Service and estate identity projection only. Read affected AGENTS.md files, architecture ADR-0008, the completed Estate Service report, infrastructure configuration and contracts 0.2.0 first. Preserve independent Git roots and service-owned databases. Consume the Estate Service v2 snapshots with transactional consumer_name/eventId deduplication, revision-aware updates, retry/DLQ/replay and reconciliation. Implement spatial-owned PostGIS geometry and RFC 7946 WGS84 API contracts, using canonical estate/block UUIDs without cross-database access. Reject new operational use of inactive blocks and label synthetic fixtures SIMULATED. Add contract/security/PostGIS integration and duplicate/out-of-order event tests. Validate builds, migrations, permissions and Docker, document actual results and blockers, and stop after Milestone 1B. Do not add operations, telemetry, AI, web/immersive functionality or deploy to Azure.

Membership/lifecycle changes can require operator reconciliation of existing geometry.

excerpt: Preparation found these differences: foundation pom/ADR-0005 use Java 25, while the explicit request asks for Java 21; Spatial targets 21 and was fully verified on 21. head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
excerpt: Division lifecycle cannot be authoritative until Estate contracts expose it; existing geometry after lifecycle/membership changes needs reconciliation. Imports are synchronous, atomic and capped at 100 features/2 MiB by default; no CSV endpoint, background job worker, geometry repair, altitude/vertical datum, antimeridian workflow or general projected-polygon transformation is included. Explicit CRS conversion supports points in 4326/3857 only. History has a documented inline cap, exports require paging, and queries can be truncated by explicit limit. Retention, alerting, DLQ operator permissions, reconciliation scheduling, publisher lock-timeout sizing, image digest pinning and performance/load characterization remain deployment hardening tasks. Synthetic asset URLs intentionally do not resolve.
